title: Media Upload Failures
description: Fix 'HTTP error', file size limits, permission issues, and broken image uploads in the media library.

steps.title: Capture Exact Upload Error
steps.instructions: Note the browser message (HTTP error, file too large, unable to create directory). Test a small JPG vs a large PDF to narrow the cause.

steps.title: Raise upload_max_filesize and post_max_size
steps.instructions: Increase php.ini limits (e.g. 64M upload, 128M post). post_max_size must be larger than upload_max_filesize. Restart PHP after changes.

steps.title: Fix wp-content/uploads Permissions
steps.instructions: Ensure uploads directory exists with 755 permissions and is writable by the web server user. Create missing year/month subfolders if needed.

steps.title: Check Disk Space and Inode Quota
steps.instructions: Full disks or exhausted inodes cause silent upload failures. Verify hosting quota in the control panel and clean unused backups or logs.

steps.title: Check mod_security and MIME Restrictions
steps.instructions: WAF rules may block certain file types or multipart uploads. Review server error logs and whitelist WordPress admin upload paths if needed.

steps.title: Verify Image Processing Libraries
steps.instructions: WordPress needs GD or Imagick for image thumbnails. Install missing PHP extensions and confirm memory is sufficient for large images.

steps.title: Test Upload and Display
steps.instructions: Upload images, PDFs, and a video if allowed. Confirm thumbnails generate and files display correctly on the front end.
